newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore offers perks to boost stock, debt markets.
newsitem.headline: Singapore offers perks to boost stock, debt markets.

text.p: Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu unveiled on Friday a series of tax incentives to boost Singapore's foreign currency denominated share market and debt market.

Hu said in his budget speech banks would not be taxed on income earned from managing initial public offerings of foreign currency denominated shares for an initial period of five years, effective from the 1998 year of assessment.

He said income earned by Asian Currency Units (ACU) and Approved Securities Companies from trading of foreign currency denominated shares on Singapore's stock exchange would also be tax exempt for five years from the 1998 year of assessment.
To encourage borrowers to issue bonds and other debt securities in Singapore, he said all fees earned by financial institutions in arranging offshore debt issues would be exempted from tax.
Currently, only issues underwritten by Singapore-based financial institutions are tax exempt.
Hu said Singapore would also grant a concessionary tax rate of 10 percent on income earned from providing credit rating services for the issue of foreign currency denominated securities.
He said this would allow Singapore to play a pivotal role in the development of Asia's burgeoning debt market.
To qualify for the exemption, also effective for five years from 1998, a credit rating agency would need to have a 10 year track record in international credit rating.
It would also need to employ at least two qualified credit analysts in Singapore and incur annual business spending of at least S$500,000 domestically.
